title: 2006 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 11
statement: Find the largest positive integer \(n\) such that \(1!+2!+3!+\cdots+n\) ! is a perfect square. Prove that your answer is correct.

solutions.text:
Clearly \(1!+2!+3!=9\) works. For \(n \geq 4\), we have

\[1!+2!+3!+\cdots+n!\equiv 1!+2!+3!+4!\equiv 3 \quad(\bmod 5)\]

but there are no squares congruent to 3 modulo 5 .
